items.text:
Just say no. This game requires a huge time commitment to get anything done. I love the IDEA of this game, but the actual game mechanics are, in places, kind of trash.  Examples:

- Rebuild a basic starter ship and get it to a useable level of functionality? Two to four hours of game play at minimum.  
- Rebuild a medium sized ship with lots of changes once you outgrow your starter ship? Plan on loosing a couple evenings and an easy eight hours and likely many more in real life.
- Now that you have a freshly rebuilt ship that you literally dumped all of those real life hours into creating and customizing, expect the wear and maintenance mechanics to require you to touch every last component on that ship every in-game weak or so.  Cost is another hour or two of real-life time watching your character grind out queued up repairs or letting them run around randomly on autotask every couple of play sessions.
- Want to fly between planetary systems, it takes a minimum of an hour or sometimes two in real time, all the while doing nothing but having your character sleep and using the game's super fast forward mode.

So why not do something actually fun during that time instead?  The game has a completely inane mechanic that looks at how long the player had the game running in real time, and anywhere outside staring area it applies significant damage about every ten minutes. Need to do something IRL with the game paused, be prepared to get zapped once you come off the pause button.  The timed damage mechanic does not affect early game play, it only starts to pound you once have a bunch of hours invested in a play-through and want to move beyond the starting game-play loop. This is why most players will never really be impacted by it before they write a review.

There are some other issues as well.

- Your crew feel like giving orders to "Dwarf Fortress" dwarves from like 10-15 years ago; you cannot actually trust them to reliably keep themselves alive, although they mostly kind of do what you ask.  You will also need to make sure your toddler crew gets their food, water, goes potty, and goes beddie-bye.
- The ship salvage and building/rebuilding part of the game has very clicky mechanics, and in the latest pre-release those mechanics went from bad to worse. You used to just have to focus and interact with a series of tiny sections on the screen while the rest was covered in graphical clutter. Now they "improved" that by reducing the graphical clutter, but also taking what was already a clicky, grindy mess and making it even slower and more unreliable for item placement.
- The space and orbital mechanics are .. um ...interesting?  If you were hoping for KSP or X4 style flight mechanics this will not deliver.  Space is a flat 2d, and the orbital mechanics seem to be hard coded as opposed to physics driven.  Parts of this are fun, but discard any sim thinking at the title screen.

The early game is a lot of fun, and well worth the price of entry.  Once past that the game-play quality goes way down and gets grindy with bad mechanics.  Hopefully the dev team figures things out and goes back to finding the fun this game has the potential to offer.

Finally let's talk bugs:
There is not one single game-play mechanic in this game that is not subject problematic behavior and things occasionally not working as expected. Yes, the game is early access and some of this is expected.  But even in early access I would expect some systems to be bug free. I have yet to experience one in this game. Unfortunately that also means that while most game breaking bugs are being or have been addressed, even those still show up with surprising regularity in unexpected times and places. Play the game long enough and even on the latest builds you will hit things that for you to reload back to a save and loose game advancement. I have never played a single session where I've been in the game for more than an hour or so with encountering at least minor bugs that routinely frustrate me.

I really want the game to mature and succeed, it does have a lot of potential. It may require some adult guidance to get there.
items.text_zh:
直接说不吧。这款游戏需要投入大量时间才能做成任何事。我喜欢这款游戏的理念，但实际的游戏机制在某些地方简直就是垃圾。例如：

- 重建一艘基础的新手船并让它达到可用的功能水平？至少需要两到四个小时的游戏时间。
- 当你不再满足于新手船后，重建一艘有大量改动的中型飞船？准备好失去几个晚上，轻松花上八个小时，在现实生活中很可能还要多得多。
- 现在你有一艘刚刚重建好的飞船，你确实把那些现实生活中的小时全都倾注在创建和定制它上面了，那就等着磨损和维护机制要求你每隔一个游戏内星期左右就得触碰那艘船上的每一个部件吧。代价是再花一两个小时的现实时间，看着你的角色把排队的修理任务磨完，或者每隔几次游戏就让它们在自动任务下到处乱跑。
- 想在行星系之间飞行？至少需要一个小时，有时是两个小时的现实时间，全程除了让你的角色睡觉、使用游戏的超快进模式之外什么也做不了。

那为什么不在这段时间里做点真正有趣的事呢？游戏有一个完全荒唐的机制，它会查看玩家让游戏在现实时间中运行了多久，而在起始区域之外的任何地方，它大约每十分钟就会施加一次可观的伤害。需要在游戏暂停时去做现实中的事情？准备好一旦你松开暂停键就被电一下吧。这个定时伤害机制不影响早期游戏，只有当你已经在一个存档里投入了大量小时、想要超越起始游戏循环时，它才开始猛击你。这就是为什么大多数玩家在写评测之前永远不会真正受到它的影响。

还有一些其他问题。

- 你的船员感觉就像在给大约10到15年前的《矮人要塞》矮人下命令；你不能真正信任他们能可靠地保住自己的命，尽管他们大体上还算会做你要求的事。你还得确保你的幼儿船员们有饭吃、有水喝、去上厕所、乖乖上床睡觉。
- 游戏的飞船打捞和建造/重建部分有着非常依赖点击的机制，而在最新的预发布版中，那些机制从糟糕变得更糟。以前你只需要集中注意力，与屏幕上的一系列微小区域互动，而其余部分则被图形杂乱物覆盖。现在他们通过减少图形杂乱物来“改进”了这一点，但同时也把原本就已经是点击、刷磨的烂摊子变得更慢，物品放置也更不可靠。
- 太空和轨道力学……嗯……挺有意思？如果你期待的是KSP或X4风格的飞行力学，这款游戏不会满足你。太空是平面的2D，轨道力学似乎是硬编码的，而不是物理驱动的。其中有些部分很有趣，但在标题画面就把任何模拟游戏的思维丢掉吧。

早期游戏非常有趣，完全值回入场价。一旦过了那个阶段，游戏质量就大幅下降，变得又刷又磨，机制还很糟糕。希望开发团队能搞清楚状况，回到寻找这款游戏有潜力提供的乐趣上来。

最后来说说bug：
这款游戏里没有任何一个游戏机制不存在问题行为，也不存在偶尔不按预期运作的情况。是的，游戏是抢先体验版，其中一些是意料之中的。但即便在抢先体验版中，我也会期望有些系统是没有bug的。我还没有在这款游戏中体验到一个。不幸的是，这也意味着虽然大多数破坏游戏的bug正在被解决或已经被解决，但即便是那些bug仍然会以惊人的频率在意想不到的时间和地点出现。玩得够久，即便在最新的版本上，你也会撞上一些让你不得不读档重来、损失游戏进度的事情。我从来没有玩过一次超过一小时左右的游戏会话而不遇到至少一些经常让我感到沮丧的小bug。

我真的很希望这款游戏能成熟并成功，它确实有很大潜力。可能需要一些成年人的指导才能走到那一步。

我真的很希望这游戏能成熟并成功，它确实有很大的潜力。它可能需要一些成年人的引导才能达到那一步。
